author: titoma1500
body:
**Descripción:**
Este pull request implementa la integración dinámica de la misión, visión y autoridades de la facultad, conectando correctamente el backend y frontend a la base de datos real, conforme a la tabla facultad en Prisma. A continuación se detallan los cambios realizados:

Backend:

Eliminación del uso de la API ficticia de configuración: Se eliminó el controlador y las rutas de configuración (configuracion.controller.js y configuracion.routes.js), ya que no se utilizaban en otros módulos.

Nuevos Endpoints en facultad.controller.js:

GET /api/facultades/:id: Endpoint para obtener la misión y visión de la facultad.

PUT /api/facultades/:id: Endpoint para actualizar la misión y visión, restringido solo a usuarios con rol ADMIN.

Los cambios realizados en la base de datos se validan correctamente.

Frontend:

Modificación de AdminConfiguracion.jsx:

Se conectó la edición de la misión y visión directamente a los endpoints de facultad, eliminando las referencias a /api/configuracion.

Se implementaron validaciones y manejo de errores para mostrar mensajes claros al administrador.

Observación sobre el ID de la facultad: Se asumió que el ID de la facultad está disponible desde el backend, pero en el frontend, se utiliza un valor predeterminado para facultadActual.id. Este valor debe ser actualizado según la lógica de autenticación o recuperación del ID de la facultad del usuario en el futuro. Es importante revisar este detalle con el equipo si es necesario ajustarlo en futuras implementaciones.

Visualización Dinámica: La misión y visión ahora se actualizan dinámicamente en el frontend, con los valores obtenidos del backend.

Vista Pública (Home.jsx):

Visualización de Misión y Visión: Los valores de misión y visión ahora se obtienen de la base de datos real y se muestran dinámicamente en la página pública, reflejando los cambios realizados por el administrador.

Validaciones y Seguridad:

Restricción de edición solo a administradores: Ya se encontraba implementado y se validó que solo los usuarios con rol ADMIN puedan editar la misión y visión.

Se validó que los campos de misión y visión no estén vacíos antes de ser guardados.

Observaciones adicionales:

Facultad ID: En el archivo Home.jsx, el ID de la facultad (facultadActual.id) está configurado actualmente como un valor fijo (1). Este ID debe ser dinámico, dependiendo de la facultad asociada al usuario o contexto. Es importante ajustar esto para reflejar correctamente la facultad del usuario en la vista pública, según sea necesario.

Carrera y Facultad: Si en el futuro se requiere acceder a las carreras asociadas a la facultad (como mencionamos con las carreras), se debe revisar el modelo de carrera en el frontend para asegurarse de que la información esté sincronizada adecuadamente entre el backend y el frontend.

Criterios de Aceptación:

Misión, visión y autoridades ahora se editan y consultan desde la tabla real facultad en la base de datos.

El frontend y backend están correctamente integrados.

Los cambios realizados se reflejan en la vista pública de la facultad.

Solo los administradores pueden editar la misión y visión.

Se implementaron validaciones y manejo de errores para una mejor experiencia del usuario.

Cierre de la Issue:
Este PR cierra la issue #44.

Adds craftable arrows and bolts that extinguish flames.

Water vial arrow/bolt
An arrow, an alchemical vial and a bit of fiber with crafting skill.

The CI workflow was failing due to 19 line length violations across 10 files in `docs/references/SLAU455/`, where technical descriptions from Texas Instruments documentation exceeded the 120-character limit configured in `.markdownlint.jsonc`.

## Solution
Fixed all line length violations by breaking long lines at natural points while preserving the exact technical content and intent from the original TI documentation:

- Split long sentences at logical boundaries (commas, conjunctions)
- Maintained all technical accuracy and terminology
- Preserved code examples and technical descriptions exactly as documented
- No functional changes to any implementation code

- ✅ All markdownlint checks now pass
- ✅ All existing tests continue to pass

- ✅ Content preservation verified through diff review

This PR fixes a build issue where the OpenAI client was being initialized at module level, causing build failures when the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable is not set during build time.

### 🔧 Changes Made

- **Moved OpenAI client initialization** from module level to inside the request handler
- **Prevents build-time errors** when API key is not configured
- **Maintains proper error handling** for missing API key at runtime
- **Ensures successful builds** without requiring API key during build process

### 🎯 Problem Solved

**Before**: Build would fail with error:
```
Error: The OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable is missing or empty
```

**After**: Build succeeds regardless of API key presence, with proper runtime error handling.

### ✅ Testing

- ✅ Build succeeds without API key set
- ✅ Runtime error handling works when API key is missing
- ✅ AI chat functions properly when API key is configured
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality

### 📋 Technical Details

**File Changed**: `src/app/api/chat/route.ts`

**Change**: Moved this code from module level to inside the POST handler:
```typescript
const openai = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY,
});
```

This ensures the OpenAI client is only initialized when the API endpoint is actually called, not during the build process.

### 🚀 Impact

- **Improved Developer Experience**: No need to set API key just to build the app
- **Better CI/CD**: Build pipelines work without API key configuration
- **Proper Error Handling**: Clear runtime errors when API key is missing
- **No Functional Changes**: AI features work exactly the same when properly configured

---

This is a small but important fix that improves the development and deployment experience while maintaining all existing functionality.

body:
This PR implements the complete UI layer for habit management, including screens for displaying habits and adding/editing habits using Compose Multiplatform with MVVM architecture.

## 🚀 Features Implemented

### Habit List Screen
- **HabitListScreen**: Complete Compose UI for displaying all user habits
- **HabitListViewModel**: State management with loading, error, and success states
- Displays habit name, description, color indicator, and active status
- Empty state guidance and error handling with retry functionality
- Material Design 3 components with floating action button for adding habits

### Habit Edit Screen  
- **HabitEditScreen**: Form interface for creating and editing habits
- **HabitEditViewModel**: Form state management with real-time validation
- Form fields: name (required), description (optional), color selection, active status
- Color palette with 10 predefined options and visual selection feedback
- Input validation with inline error messages and save state management

## 🏗️ Architecture

### MVVM Pattern Implementation
- **ViewModels**: Manage UI state using `StateFlow` for reactive updates
- **Unidirectional Data Flow**: User actions → ViewModel → State updates → UI recomposition
- **Separation of Concerns**: ViewModels communicate with domain layer through use cases only

### Dependency Injection
- Updated Koin modules for all layers (domain, data, presentation)
- ViewModels properly inject required use cases (`GetAllHabitsUseCase`, `AddHabitUseCase`)
- Clean dependency flow following dependency inversion principle

## 🧪 Testing

### Comprehensive Unit Tests
- **HabitListViewModelTest**: 4 test cases covering state management, error handling, and refresh functionality
- **HabitEditViewModelTest**: 10 test cases covering form validation, save operations, and error scenarios
- All 36 tests passing in CI workflow
- Mock-based testing using MockK with coroutine test support

### Test Coverage
```kotlin
// Example test demonstrating ViewModel behavior
@Test
fun `saveHabit should succeed with valid data`() = runTest {
    // Given valid form data
    viewModel.updateName("Morning Exercise")
    viewModel.updateDescription("30 minutes workout")
    
    // When saving
    viewModel.saveHabit(onSuccess = { id -> /* success */ })
    
    // Then use case is called with correct data
    coVerify { mockAddHabitUseCase(match { habit ->
        habit.name == "Morning Exercise" && 
        habit.description == "30 minutes workout"
    })}
}
```

## 📚 Documentation

### Screen Specifications (`docs/SPECIFICATIONS.md`)
- Detailed specifications for both screens including purpose, UI components, and user interactions
- Form validation rules and behavior documentation  
- Color palette specifications and accessibility considerations

### Architecture Documentation (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`)
- Enhanced presentation layer section with MVVM pattern explanation
- ViewModel responsibilities and state management patterns
- Dependency injection setup and unidirectional data flow description

## 🎯 User Experience

### Habit List Screen
- Clean list view with Material Design 3 cards
- Color-coded habit indicators for visual organization
- Loading states and error handling with user-friendly messages
- Empty state guidance encouraging first habit creation

### Habit Edit Screen  
- Intuitive form layout with clear field labels and validation
- Visual color selection with highlight indicators
- Real-time validation feedback
- Save/cancel navigation with loading states

## 🔧 Technical Implementation

### State Management
```kotlin
data class HabitListUiState(
    val habits: List<Habit> = emptyList(),
    val isLoading: Boolean = false,
    val error: String? = null
)
```

### Reactive UI Updates
```kotlin
@Composable
fun HabitListScreen(viewModel: HabitListViewModel) {
    val uiState by viewModel.uiState.collectAsState()
    
    when {
        uiState.isLoading -> LoadingIndicator()
        uiState.error != null -> ErrorState(uiState.error)
        else -> HabitList(uiState.habits)
    }
}
```

Fixes #9.

author: lukehankey
body:
Based on the new design for the dialog box which looks like the mobile version, this is somewhat of a quick hack to get it working with the Tesseract OCR reader.

- Must use the alt1 key press to work
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/815b5975-0e93-4623-be67-4049c0caa9c6)

I didn't even know this was a thing but needless to say, this isn't supported in the default alt1. Since the code uses Tesseract for the OCR instead of the alt1 built-in OCR reader, there is a little bit more flexibility. The key thing to this though is that this always appears at the bottom of the screen, so with a sensible screen size, the reader can always detect the text at the bottom. As for being specific to the Misty dialog text, I have chosen to go with the manual alt + 1 key press.

Other options I explored:
- Try the same OCR reader to capture the Misty title but this is more dynamic than the text due to the chat head moving when the client is resized.
- Using the chat head as a template and comparing images which seemed like it would work but was too much effort 😆 to even get set up in development.

## Description

This PR adds the initial configuration for Codecov via the `codecov.yml` file.

The goal is to improve the visibility of code coverage directly on pull requests by customizing the PR comment layout. The configuration includes:

* Showing the coverage diff and per-file coverage
* Displaying the total coverage of the head and base branches
* Including a tree overview of directory-level coverage
* Always posting a comment even if coverage hasn’t changed
* Ensuring comments are only posted when a coverage report is present

These changes aim to provide a clearer overview of how each PR impacts test coverage across the project, helping maintain a high-quality and well-tested codebase.

body: ## Motivation A certain someone often times out a certain other someone, and since officers by default do not have timeout && audit log permissions, they can't see when it happens & who did it. ## Overview This listener just broadcasts the timeout event to the bot logs channel, and if it was an officer that was timed out, the officer memes channel as well (for the meme). Some code shamelessly ripped off from my other Discord bot project. Example embeds: > [!WARNING] > > To make this feature work, the bot's privilege has been elevated in the following ways: > - Gateway intents: Enabled the [`GUILD_MODERATION` bit](https://discord.com/developers/docs/events/gateway#list-of-intents). > - Role permissions: Enabled **View Audit Log**. > - Channel access overwrites: Enabled **View Channel** for the bot role for the officer memes channel.

body:
## 📑 Description

Closes https://github.com/goravel/goravel/issues/704

<!-- Please add Review Ready tag or leave a Review Ready message when the PR is good to go -->
<!-- More description can be written after this -->

This pull request refactors the Redis cache implementation and its associated tests. The changes include renaming and simplifying the Redis client creation logic, updating the cache test suite to use a more modular structure, and replacing the `supportredis` package with a local implementation. The most important changes are grouped below by theme:

### Redis Client Refactoring
* Renamed `support/redis/connection.go` to `client.go` and replaced `GetClient` with a private `getClient` function for Redis client retrieval. This function now uses a simplified configuration prefix (`configPrefix`) for clarity. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4b667feae66c9d46b21b9ecc19e8958cf4472d162ce0a47ac3e8386af8bbd8cfL11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4b667feae66c9d46b21b9ecc19e8958cf4472d162ce0a47ac3e8386af8bbd8cfL25-R33) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4b667feae66c9d46b21b9ecc19e8958cf4472d162ce0a47ac3e8386af8bbd8cfL44-R42) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-4b667feae66c9d46b21b9ecc19e8958cf4472d162ce0a47ac3e8386af8bbd8cfL64-R66)

### Cache Implementation Updates
* Updated the `Cache` struct in `cache.go` to use the new `getClient` function instead of the removed `supportredis.GetClient`. This eliminates the dependency on the `supportredis` package.

### Test Suite Improvements
* Refactored `cache_test.go` to modularize the setup and teardown logic using `SetupSuite` and `TearDownSuite` methods. This includes initializing Docker and mocking Redis configurations. ## 🎯 Feature: Proper Idea History Timeline Viewer

### Problem
The current "View Full History" button was just dumping text into the chat, making it difficult to:
- See timestamps for each version
- Navigate between different versions
- Understand the evolution of the idea visually
- Access specific iterations from the database

### Solution
Created a beautiful modal-based idea history viewer that shows:
- ✅ **Visual Timeline** - Clear timeline with dots and connectors
- ✅ **Timestamps** - When each version was created (e.g., "3 hours ago")
- ✅ **Version Details** - Click any version to see the full content at that point
- ✅ **Change Types** - Color-coded badges (refinement, major revision, branch, merge)
- ✅ **AI Confidence** - Shows the AI's confidence score for each update
- ✅ **Current Version** - Highlighted at the top with a star icon

### Changes Made
1. Created new `IdeaHistoryModal.tsx` component with:
   - Timeline visualization
   - Version cards with metadata
   - Click-to-view version details
   - Responsive design

2. Updated `ChatInterface.tsx` to:
   - Import and use the new modal
   - Add state management for the modal
   - Replace text-based history with modal trigger

### User Experience
- Click "View Full History" or type `/history` → Opens beautiful timeline modal
- See all versions at a glance with timestamps and change summaries
- Click any version to view the full content at that point in time
- Clear visual indicators for different types of changes

### Screenshots
The modal shows:
- Current version prominently at the top
- Timeline with connected dots for each version
- Clickable cards with version details
- Clean, modern UI that matches the app's design

### Testing
1. Go to Ideas Gallery and develop an existing idea
2. Click "View Full History" button or type `/history`
3. Modal should open showing the timeline
4. Click on any version to see details
5. Close modal and verify

Thanks for your work on this package, very useful!

I'd like to suggest adding a customizable fallback CSL style variable: `org-cite-csl-activate-fallback-style`. 

This can be used either to affect all org documents, or when set alongside `org-cite-csl-activate-use-document-style`, as a fallback for documents without a style set within the document, e.g.
```
(setq org-cite-csl-activate-use-document-style t
        org-cite-csl-activate-fallback-style "apa.csl"))
```

Currently by default the fallback style is determined by oc-csl.el, where it's hard coded as Chicago author-date. The default style for export can be changed with `org-cite-export-processors` — this new variable makes it possible to do the same for org-cite-csl-activate.

I have read the CLA Document and I sign the CLA

This PR addressess the issue #20974 (references #6043)

## Description 

Adds size-specific mAP metrics (`map_small`, `map_medium`, `map_large`) to the `Metric` class, making them programmatically accessible through `Metric.box.map_small`, `Metric.box.map_medium`, and `Metric.box.map_large`.

## Changes Made

- **Added `size_specific_metrics` list** to `Metric` class initialization with default values `[0.0, 0.0, 0.0]`
- **Added three new properties** to `Metric` class:
  - `map_small`: Returns mAP for small objects (IoU 0.5-0.95)
  - `map_medium`: Returns mAP for medium objects (IoU 0.5-0.95)  
  - `map_large`: Returns mAP for large objects (IoU 0.5-0.95)
- **Added `update_size_metrics()` method** for updating values from COCO evaluation
- **Modified `eval_json()` in `DetectionValidator`** to capture COCO evaluator stats[3:6] and populate size-specific metrics
- **Added comprehensive tests** in `tests/test_size_metrics.py` covering:
  - Unit tests for `Metric` class functionality
  - Integration tests for COCO and non-COCO scenarios
  - Property validation and update mechanisms

## Testing

- [x] **COCO datasets**: Size-specific metrics populate with real values from COCO evaluator
- [x] **Non-COCO datasets**: Metrics default to 0.0 as expected
- [x] **Unit tests**: All 5 tests pass, covering initialization, updates, and properties
- [x] **Integration tests**: COCO validation pipeline works correctly  
- [x] **Backward compatibility**: Existing metrics unchanged and working
- [x] **API verification**: Confirmed access via `results.box.map_small`, `results.box.map_medium`, `results.box.map_large`

## Usage Example

```python
from ultralytics import YOLO

# Load model and train 
model = YOLO("yolo11n.pt")
results = model.train(data="coco.yaml")

# Access size-specific metrics (COCO datasets)
print(f"Small objects mAP: {results.box.map_small:.3f}")
print(f"Medium objects mAP: {results.box.map_medium:.3f}")  
print(f"Large objects mAP: {results.box.map_large:.3f}")

# For non-COCO datasets, values default to 0.0
results_yolo = model.val(data="custom_yolo_dataset.yaml")
print(f"Small objects mAP: {results_yolo.box.map_small}")  # 0.0
```

## 🛠️ PR Summary

<sub>Made with ❤️ by [Ultralytics Actions](https://github.com/ultralytics/actions)<sub>

### 🌟 Summary
Adds size-specific mAP metrics (small/medium/large) to YOLO detection validation, exposing `map_small`, `map_medium`, and `map_large` when evaluating on COCO datasets. 📏📦

### 📊 Key Changes
- New size-specific metrics in `Metric`:
  - Properties: `map_small`, `map_medium`, `map_large`
  - Storage: `size_specific_metrics = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]`
  - Method: `update_size_metrics(map_small, map_medium, map_large)`
- COCO integration in `DetectionValidator.eval_json`:
  - Automatically extracts and updates size-specific AP values from COCO evaluation when available.
- Tests added:
  - Unit tests for initialization, updates, and property correctness.
  - Integration test (COCO-only, requires `pycocotools`) validating metrics are populated.
  - Default behavior test ensuring non-COCO datasets return 0.0 for size metrics.

### 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- Better insights: Users can now analyze model performance by object size (small/medium/large) on COCO. 🔍
- Backward compatible: No breaking API changes; defaults remain 0.0 for non-COCO datasets.
- Easier benchmarking: Facilitates fine-grained evaluation and model comparison, especially for datasets with varied object scales.
- Quick usage example:
  ```python
  from ultralytics import YOLO

  model = YOLO("yolo11n.pt")
  results = model.val(data="coco8.yaml", imgsz=640)
  print(results.metrics.box.map_small, results.metrics.box.map_medium, results.metrics.box.map_large)
  ```
  Note: Size metrics are populated for COCO; non-COCO datasets will return 0.0.

author: luohaha
body:
## Why I'm doing:
In previous PR #58923 , we introduced bundle data file feature.
And in the current implementation, there are several issues that may cause bundled data file reading failures:
1. During multi-partition imports, bundled data files may be shared across partitions. Since data files cannot exist across partition directories, this causes the system to fail locating the bundled files.
2. Preloading initiated before bundled data files are fully persisted results in "file not found" errors.
3. Incorrect usage of bundled data file reading APIs in multiple code paths leads to data reading anomalies.

## What I'm doing:
Fix #58316
This PR fixes the aforementioned issues. 

### Enhancements for Bundling Data Files:

* **New Method for Checking Bundling Status**: Added `_is_data_file_bundle_enabled` method in `LakeTabletsChannel` to encapsulate logic for determining whether data file bundling is enabled based on request parameters. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-cb0fbac7cd7174aa5fccc214e7e862f79a8e11a9666c0fa36a8205ab4d09fcb5R209-R210)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cb0fbac7cd7174aa5fccc214e7e862f79a8e11a9666c0fa36a8205ab4d09fcb5R668-R672)`)
* **Partition-Based Bundling Context**: Replaced the single `BundleWritableFileContext` with a partition-based mapping (`_bwfile_ctxs_by_partition`) to manage bundled files more effectively. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-cb0fbac7cd7174aa5fccc214e7e862f79a8e11a9666c0fa36a8205ab4d09fcb5L238-R241)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cb0fbac7cd7174aa5fccc214e7e862f79a8e11a9666c0fa36a8205ab4d09fcb5R710-R716)`)
* **Delta Writer Updates**: Modified `_create_delta_writers` to use partition-specific bundling contexts and updated the `DeltaWriter` builder to support bundled files. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-cb0fbac7cd7174aa5fccc214e7e862f79a8e11a9666c0fa36a8205ab4d09fcb5R710-R716)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cb0fbac7cd7174aa5fccc214e7e862f79a8e11a9666c0fa36a8205ab4d09fcb5L726-R737)`)

### File Handling Improvements:

* **File Access Updates**: Replaced `new_random_access_file` with `new_random_access_file_with_bundling` in multiple locations to accommodate bundled file handling. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a5433fc4c5ee849e918b1c2eb9974d5aecc02b3903155ed745b7c7ce6fa42461L192-R192)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3c073f242259e54f685bafc4fd19da86b21969be5de8ae5b81ca0a4ee451c325L43-R43)`)
* **Skip Preload Logic**: Enhanced `DeltaWriterImpl` to skip primary key preload when bundled files are present, ensuring correct handling of unflushed data. (`[be/src/storage/lake/delta_writer.cppL616-R618](diffhunk://#diff-24e44403f5e4c75144f9645f2fcff77dcdd9269836bafd5b79d5b2d6589e49fdL616-R618)`)

### Testing:

* **New Test Case**: Added `test_write_bundling_file` in `LakeTabletsChannelTest` to validate the functionality of data file bundling, including partition handling and transaction log verification. (`[be/test/runtime/lake_tablets_channel_test.cppR444-R508](diffhunk://#diff-24bc5f1765c03c495d5cd72f1dff37877249a0f187b1b608e1010e3284b460a0R444-R508)`)

### Miscellaneous:

* **Comment Updates**: Updated comments to reflect the new bundling terminology, replacing "shared data file" with "bundle data file." (`[be/src/storage/lake/general_tablet_writer.cppL132-R132](diffhunk://#diff-3dc155c1f66ca23166df68c90b2dd007553dcdb5614809d09dc669af8d406593L132-R132)`)
* **Additional Includes**: Included `<cstdint>` in `tablet_retain_info.h` for consistency and completeness. (`[be/src/storage/lake/tablet_retain_info.hR17](diffhunk://#diff-1249fb64d433d33db81344d35f81ac9e5d933a5151bf1dc2af76bb0152163b39R17)`)

## Summary

This PR addresses **GitHub issue #253** - a critical security vulnerability where the application used weak default secret keys that could be exploited for session hijacking, CSRF token bypass, and data tampering.

## Changes Made

### 🔒 Security Improvements

1. **backend/config.py**:
   - ✅ Replaced weak fallback `'dev-secret-key'` with cryptographically secure random key generation using `secrets.token_hex(32)`
   - ✅ Added warning log when SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set
   - ✅ Maintains backward compatibility while encouraging proper production setup

2. **docker-compose.yml**:
   - ✅ Removed weak fallback `'production-secret-key-change-me'`
   - ✅ Forces explicit SECRET_KEY setting in production environments

3. **backend/security_check.py**:
   - ✅ Updated to recognize secure generated keys as acceptable fallback
   - ✅ Security check now passes with generated keys (no more false critical alerts)

4. **.env.example**:
   - ✅ Added clear instructions for generating secure SECRET_KEY using Python's secrets module

### 🛠️ Frontend Fixes

5. **frontend/src/services/cycleCountService.js**:

## Security Impact

### Before (Vulnerable)
- Predictable secret keys: `'dev-secret-key'` and `'production-secret-key-change-me'`
- Session hijacking risk through brute-force attacks
- CSRF token bypass potential
- Data integrity compromise

### After (Secure)
- Cryptographically secure 64-character random keys
- Session security maintained with unpredictable keys


author: ernieblues
body:
@johnhenley 

I was able to reproduce the duplicate topic tracking issue once by double-clicking a topic link, but it's a rare event and I have not been able to trigger it again. It looks like the duplicate record only gets inserted when there’s some latency between reading and writing to the topics tracking table. My investigation was focused on the topic tracking table while assuming the forum tracking table was exhibiting the same behavior. I simulated the database latency and was able to reliably reproduce the issue.

The changes to `08.02.04.SqlDataProvider` and `TopicView.cs` are for testing purposes only. The issue can be toggled by commenting/uncommenting the 250 ms delay. When the delay is active, the fix can be toggled by commenting/uncommenting the debounce method. I appreciate your input.

## Potential fixes
- Prevent double-clicking any topic or forum links. I have included the debounce method that can be uncommented for testing.
- I attempted to wrap the procedure in a serializable transaction, but it resulted in a deadlock.
- Adding a unique constraint to the table is another option, but that would catch the error _after_ it occurs and would have to fail silently. Also, as noted in the issue, the tables would have to be cleaned up before an upgrade installation.

## Changes made
- `TopicView.cs`: Commented out the cache access to allow repeated inserts.
- `08.02.04.SqlDataProvider`: Added a 250 ms simulated latency.
  _Note: Requires a full uninstall or manual procedure update in SSMS._
- `afcommon.js`: Added link debounce method (uncomment to test possible fix).

## How did you test these updates?  
- Created a forum with several topics.
- Double-clicked a topic link.
- Monitored the activeforums_Topics_Tracking table for inserted records.
- Deleted the records and repeated the double-click test.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code documentation](http://docs.anthropic.com/s/claude-code-github-actions).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: tejhan
body:
This PR introduces a validation step for the active kubeconfig path. When the configured file cannot be found, the extension now alerts the user and offers to add or select a new kubeconfig. Before this change, invalid or missing kubeconfig paths caused the extension to fail silently, leaving the cluster tree view empty and users unaware that their configuration was the issue.

This update covers scenarios where users carry over a kubeconfig path from another machine and forget to update it, as well as cases where the extension falls back to default locations on a fresh install. In both situations, instead of showing a blank cluster menu, the extension will now prompt the user to correct their kubeconfig location immediately.

Related issues: 
#1333, #1334, #1418

(Note: these issues all have their own nuances but each has similar issue of not being notified when the actively set kubeconfig is non-existent.)

## 概要

このプルリクエストは、cargo testエラーの修正と並列実行対応のテストコンテナ実装を行います。

## 修正内容

### 1. ビルド依存関係の解決
- OpenSSLとProtocol Buffersの依存関係エラーを修正
- 必要なシステムパッケージのインストール手順を明確化

### 2. テストインフラストラクチャの改善
- **TestRepositoryFactory**: 環境自動検出機能付きのテストファクトリを実装
- **環境フォールバック**: Dockerが利用できない場合のin-memory実装への自動切り替え
- **テストマクロ**: 3種類のテストマクロ（integration_test!, postgres_only_test!, in_memory_only_test!）を提供

### 3. 並列実行サポート
- テストの独立性を保証
- コンテナの適切な分離
- リソースの自動クリーンアップ

### 4. エラーハンドリングの改善
- PostgreSQL接続のリトライロジック強化
- タイムアウト処理の実装
- 詳細なエラーメッセージの提供

## テスト結果

- **単体テスト**: ✅ 94個すべて成功
- **統合テスト**: ✅ 環境に応じて適切に実行
- **ビルド**: ✅ 正常にコンパイル完了

## 新機能

### TestRepositoryFactory
```rust
// 環境自動検出
let factory = TestRepositoryFactory::new().await;

// 特定環境の強制指定
let factory = TestRepositoryFactory::with_environment(TestEnvironment::InMemory);
```

### テストマクロ
```rust
// 利用可能な最適環境で実行
integration_test!(test_crud_operations, |factory| async move {
    let repo = factory.create_item_repository();
    // テスト実装...
});

// PostgreSQL専用テスト
postgres_only_test!(test_postgres_features, |factory| async move {
    // PostgreSQL固有のテスト...
});
```

## ドキュメント

詳細な改善内容は `TESTING_IMPROVEMENTS.md` を参照してください。

## 影響範囲

- 既存のテストコードに影響なし
- 新しいテストインフラストラクチャは段階的に導入可能
- Docker環境の有無に関わらずテスト実行可能

## 今後の改善予定

- Docker自動インストール機能
- CI/CD環境での最適化
- パフォーマンステストとの統合

author: z1lk
body:
This follows the pattern set in #298. It was supposed to close #296, but I'm still seeing an issue there after upgrading to 2.3.1. It seems that `Phlex::Rails::Buffered` is not used for the adapted form builders, `Phlex::Rails::Builder` is, after #291. I've basically updated `Builder` to match `Buffered` in how it reports its own class, and added tests for both.

Additionally, I extracted the "type" methods to a `Phlex::Rails::Types` module that `Phlex::Rails` extends just after setting up the Zeitwerk loader. Defining the type methods alongside the class definitions resulted in a problem where those methods were not available until the class had been loaded. So e.g. in development `prop :form, Phlex::Rails::Builder(ActionView::Helpers::FormBuilder)` would result in `undefined method 'Builder' for Phlex::Rails:Module` unless `Phlex::Rails::Builder` was called prior, which I had no reason to do. Maybe there's a better way to handle this, but this got things working.

author: ericguan04
body:
**Liquid tracking issue:** The liquid tracking mechanism for aspiration and dispensing operations is not functioning as expected.

Through testing, it seems like `aspirate96` does not actually reduce the liquid level in the plate after aspiration. This leads to inconsistencies in the tracked liquid volume and causes errors when subsequent dispensing operations are performed, as the system believes there is more liquid available than there actually is.

Example: Assuming a plate with 360 ul volume limit, following this procedure:
* aspirate96 takes 360 ul from plate_1 (plate has 0 ul)
* dispense96 drops 360 ul to plate_1 (plate has 360 ul)
* aspirate96 takes 360 ul from plate_1 (aspirate thinks that plate has 0 ul, but dispense thinks that plate has 360 ul left --> seems to be a local/global mismatch since it did not remove the dispense96 liquid)
* dispense96 drops 360 ul to plate_1 (error because no space left)
* aspirate96 takes 360 ul from plate_1 (error beause no liquid left)

Looking through the code, it turns out that aspirate96 had some tracking code outside the tracking conditional, and dispense96 has no tracking conditional at all. I believe this is the cause for the mismatch and subsequently the errors. After implementing the changes below, the code works as intended. 
**As a side note:** If liquid tracking is enabled, it is now necessary to use `.set_well_liquids()` prior or else there will be no liquid to aspirate (wasn't the case before). I personally believe that this change makes more sense if tracking liquid is a main concern. This does cause some test cases to fail, and it's perhaps because that `.set_well_liquids()` was not used.

Additionally, enabling and disabling volume had some issues. First, for the aspirate96 and dispense96 functions, I removed the second conditional `...or not does_volume_tracking()` since it makes it much harder to turn off volume tracking (just using `.disable_volume_trackers()` would be enough). I also added a condition to ignore lids for the enable/disable volume tracking commands.

I did a good amount of testing with aspirating and dispensing, but I am not too sure about any downstream affects for other functions.

body: ### Features and Changes Dimensions, which were previously scoped globally across an organization, can now be scoped to specific projects. - Closes #3852 ```mermaid graph TD A[Start: Create or Edit Dimension] --> B{Is this a new Dimension?} B -- Yes --> C{Is Data Source in All Projects?} C -- Yes --> D[Allow dimension in All Projects or any subset of user-permitted projects] C -- No --> E{Is selected project list a subset of Data Source’s projects?} E -- Yes --> F[Allow creation] E -- No --> G[Reject creation: must align with Data Source projects] B -- No --> H[Editing existing Dimension] H --> I{Is Dimension scoped to All Projects?} I -- Yes --> J[Allow updates without strict validation] I -- No --> K{If changing projects, are the new ones subset of Data Source’s projects?} K -- Yes --> L[Allow update] K -- No --> M[Reject: invalid project assignment] H --> N{Has Data Source’s project list changed?} N -- Yes --> O[Dimension retains original project list] O --> P{User removes a project from Dimension} P -- Yes --> Q{Is the removed project still in Data Source?} Q -- Yes --> R[Allow re-add] Q -- No --> S[Cannot re-add unless Data Source regains that project] ``` ## Testing ### Creation (Happy Paths) - Create a SQL/User dimension via a data source in `"All Projects"`, scoped to: - `"All Projects"` - A subset of permitted projects (e.g. A & B) - Create a new dimension via a data source in `"All Projects"`, scoped across multiple projects (A & B) only if the user has permissions. ### Creation (Error Cases) - Attempt to scope to `"All Projects"` when the data source is project‑specific → **submit error** - Attempt to scope to an unrelated project (e.g. C) → project not listed in the dropdown - If the data source’s scopes change (e.g. Project B removed): - Editing still shows Projects A & B. - After removing B manually, re‑adding it is disallowed unless the data source is reassigned to B. ### Editing (Happy Paths) - Update an existing dimension scoped to `"All Projects"`, regardless of the data source’s current scope. - Edit a global dimension and narrow its scope to any subset of the data source’s current projects. ### Permissions - **List‑view visibility**: - Dimensions in projects where the user lacks **read** access are hidden. - If a dimension spans multiple projects and one is inaccessible, show a tooltip on that project pill. - **“Create Dimension” CTA**: - Only visible when: - The org isn’t using config files. - The user has `canCreateDimension` permission in the active project (or globally if no project selected). --- ### Screenshots Thanks to @mknowlton89 (#3344) for reference! ✌️

body:
## Summary

  Integrates the Cobra CLI framework and establishes a production-ready command structure with proper error
  handling, testing, and version management.

  ## What's Changed

  - Added Cobra v1.9.1 as the CLI framework dependency
  - Implemented root command with help text and proper metadata
  - Created version subcommand with build-time variable injection support
  - Updated Makefile ldflags to inject version info into the correct package path
  - Added comprehensive unit tests for CLI commands
  - Updated README with basic usage examples

  ## Implementation Details

  ### Package Structure
  internal/
    cli/
      root.go         # Root command definition
      root_test.go    # Command tests
      commands.go     # Command registration
      version.go      # Version subcommand
      version_test.go # Version command tests
    version/
      version.go      # Version info with ldflags injection
  cmd/
    aws-local-sync/
      main.go         # Minimal entry point with error handling

  ### Key Design Decisions

  1. **Manual Cobra implementation** (no generator) for better control
  2. **Testable architecture** with dependency injection (e.g., `io.Writer` for version command)
  3. **Clean error handling** - commands return errors, main() handles output to stderr
  4. **Proper exit codes** - 0 for success, 1 for errors
  5. **No global state** except for ldflags version injection (standard Go pattern)

  ## Testing

  - All tests pass with `go test ./...`
  - Version injection verified with `make build && ./bin/aws-local-sync version`
  - Error handling tested for invalid commands
  - Help text displays correctly when run without arguments

  ## Checklist

  - [x] Cobra framework integrated as dependency
  - [x] Root command with appropriate metadata
  - [x] Version subcommand with build metadata support
  - [x] Proper exit code handling
  - [x] Error output to stderr
  - [x] Testable command structure
  - [x] Unit tests for all commands
  - [x] No runtime panics possible
  - [x] README updated with usage examples

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code documentation](http://docs.anthropic.com/s/claude-code-github-actions).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: circushan
body:
This commit addresses an issue where the AI chatbot sometimes failed to load prescription information during payment requests and refines your interaction for selecting a payment method.

Changes include:

1.  **Simplified Payment Prompt:** In the 'initial' stage of `handle_payment_request` (in `app/services/chatbot_service.py`), after displaying the prescription details and total fee, the chatbot now directly asks you to choose a payment method: "현금으로 결제하시겠습니까, 아니면 카드로 결제하시겠습니까?" (Would you like to pay with cash or card?). This simplifies your next step.

2.  **Robust Prescription Data Handling in Confirmation Stage:** In the 'confirmation' stage of `handle_payment_request`, the system now re-fetches the prescription details (including `total_fee` and `prescription_names`) by calling `load_department_prescriptions` again. This ensures that the payment is processed using the most current and accurate data from the system, rather than relying on information potentially misremembered or incorrectly extracted by me from your confirmation message.

These changes make the payment process more robust and your interaction clearer. The risk of errors due to stale or missing prescription information during payment confirmation is significantly reduced.

author: zenithalhourlyrate
body:
This PR adds the EXTENDED encryption technique flag to the SchemeParamAttr and corresponding C++ struct. To do so the encryptionTechniqueExtended flag is moved from BGVSchemeParam to RLWESchemeParam so it could be shared among all RLWE schemes.

This is mainly meant for CKKS noise models (e.g. #1685). By default Lattigo uses the EXTENDED encryption since we always use HYBRID keyswitching for now, meanwhile OpenFHE does not support EXTENDED mode for CKKS, so there is a difference in noise modelling.

This should have no other effect on the backend, so tests are not added.

body:
This PR introduces a code-generated C api that can be used across application boundaries. This enables dynamic loading of scripts and plugins with full access to Tecs. 

New Changes:
- Add StructFunction registration to metadata for C api autogeneration
- Register C functions on main engine components like ECS, Events, Signal/EntityRefs, etc...
- Update Tecs to generate component access headers
- Add `DynamicLibrary`/`DynamicScript` system to defining scripts in a hot-reloadable DLL

- Refactor EventData type to be C-compatible using an enum + union
- Refactor ScriptManager to handle dynamic library handles and state
- Refactor C++ script definition to allow any lock type via DynamicLock
- Add cglm and dynalo dependencies for loading dynamic script dlls
- New `NamedEntity` type for a C-copyable `EntityRef` equivalent
- Set up C-compatible `TypeInfo` class for dynamic script field reflection
- Update tests to configure frame rates with new `g.LogicFPS` and `x.PhysicsFPS` cvars
- Merge Prefab and Runtime scripts into common definition, and differentiate prefab scripts with a prefixed name
- Allow scenes to define dynamic libraries to load
- Add `GuiScript` type for defining ImGui windows (not dynamically loadable yet)
- New `InlineString` and `FlatSet` types

- Change "script" component json to use "name" instead of "onTick" and "prefab"

- Fix `screenshot_diff.py` to ignore updates to the CI compiler version
- Switch many `std::string` references to `std::string_view`
- Enable filesystem callbacks on tinygltf to load non self-contained models
- Separate `ecs::Component` into `ecs::EntityComponent` and `ecs::GlobalComponent`
- Rename `Access` to `AccessMut` so function name isn't overloaded
- Fix metallic roughness override texture channels
- Use ERROR_COLOR when textures can't be loaded or are invalid
- Fix window resizing on Wayland

author: andjar
body:
This commit introduces a significant expansion of the frontend capabilities and overall user experience for the Epistol application.

Key enhancements include:

1.  **Enhanced Email Display & Interaction:**
    *   Emails in the feed now display full timestamps.
    *   Visual cues for unread emails have been added (contingent on API support for an `is_read` flag).
    *   "Reply All" and "Forward" buttons are now available for each email, with logic to pre-fill the compose modal appropriately.

2.  **Person Profiles UI:**
    *   A modal-based UI for displaying person profiles has been implemented.
    *   Sender names in the feed are now clickable (if a `sender_person_id` is available) to trigger loading and displaying profile information, including associated email threads.

3.  **Groups Management UI:**
    *   A sidebar has been added for basic group management.
    *   You can now view a list of existing groups.
    *   A form allows for creating new groups.
    *   A dropdown filter enables filtering the main email feed by selected group.

4.  **Attachment Handling UI:**
    *   Emails now display a list of their attachments with clickable download links.
    *   The compose email modal includes a file input for adding multiple attachments.
    *   The email sending mechanism has been updated to use `FormData` to support file uploads.

5.  **UI Polish & Minor Features:**
    *   Global and context-specific loading indicators have been implemented to provide feedback during API calls.
    *   Basic client-side validation has been added (e.g., for group creation).
    *   Significant CSS improvements have been made for a more polished, professional, and consistent look and feel across the application.
    *   Media queries have been added to ensure better responsiveness on various screen sizes, including mobile devices.

These changes lay a strong foundation for a feature-rich and user-friendly email client interface. Further backend integration will be required to fully enable all functionalities (e.g., `is_read` status, profile data, group operations, attachment processing).

author: alfaix
body:
Hey,
I noticed that it's not possible to render image exactly at 0,0 with window=minimal on my neovim. I think the issue is that the bounds checking is too strict, leading to (x=0, y=0)  exiting early and returning false. Repro is below, please let me know if there's something wrong with it.

<details>
<summary>Versions (Ubuntu 22.04, nvim 0.12.0-dev), wezterm 20250604</summary>

```
$ nvim --version
NVIM v0.12.0-dev-197+g1dbede5b93
Build type: Release
LuaJIT 2.1.1744317938
Run "nvim -V1 -v" for more info
$ lsb_release -a
Distributor ID: Ubuntu
Description:    Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
Release:        22.04
Codename:       jammy
$ wezterm --version
wezterm 20250604-060157-5106c8c1
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Repro</summary>
Not a very minimal one, but works. Sourcing it without the patch does not draw the image. Sourcing it with the patch does. Without the patch, setting x,y to 1,1 fixes the issue, but paints the image with an offset.

```lua
# pick up the changes on re-source
for k, _ in pairs(package.loaded) do
  if vim.startswith(k, "image") and k ~= "image" then
    package.loaded[k] = nil
  end
end

local Image = require("image")
local ImageRenderer = {}

---@return ImageRenderer
function ImageRenderer:new(parentwin, parentbuf, opts)
  local buf = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
  vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf, 0, 0, false, { "###", "###", "###", "###" })

  local obj = {
    parentbuf = parentbuf,
    parentwin = parentwin,
    height = opts.height or 10,
    width = opts.width or 20,
    bufpos = nil,
    win = nil,
    buf = buf,
    path = opts.path,
  }
  setmetatable(obj, { __index = self })
  return obj
end

function ImageRenderer:close()
  local win = self.win
  self.win = nil
  if win and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(win) then
    vim.schedule(function() pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_close, win, true) end)
  end
end

function ImageRenderer:render(pos)
  self:close()

  self.win = vim.api.nvim_open_win(self.buf, false, {
    bufpos = { pos[1], pos[2] },
    col = 0,
    focusable = true, -- FIXME
    height = self.height,
    noautocmd = true,
    relative = "win",
    row = 0,
    zindex = 11,
    style = "minimal",
    width = self.width,
    win = self.parentwin,
  })
  local image = assert(Image.from_file(self.path, {
    window = self.win,
    buffer = self.buf,
    inline = true,
  }))
  image:render({ x = 0, y = 0, width = self.width, height = self.height }) -- COORDS HERE

  local hl = "CurSearch" -- highlight to see window borders
  vim.api.nvim_set_option_value(
    "winhighlight",
    "TermCursorNC:" .. hl .. ",NormalFloat:" .. hl,
    { win = self.win }
  )
end

if _G.I ~= nil then
  _G.I:close()
end
_G.I = ImageRenderer:new(0, 0, { path = vim.fn.stdpath("config") .. "/wt.png" })
I:render({ 100, 20 })

return ImageRenderer
```

</details>
Running the above script, without changing the window spawns without an image. Changing the coordinates (at COORDS HERE) to 1,1 leads to the images below. I don't think there's a way to draw the image exactly at the border without these changes - please let me know if I'm wrong.

After:

## 📌 PR 유형 (해당하는 항목에 모두 체크해주세요)
- [ ] Feat: 새로운 기능 추가
- [x] Fix: 버그 수정
- [ ] Docs: 문서 수정
- [ ] Style: 코드 포맷팅, 세미콜론 누락, 코드 변경이 없는 경우
- [ ] Refactor: 코드 리팩토링 (기능 변경 없이 구조 개선)
- [ ] Test: 테스트 코드 추가 및 기존 테스트 리팩토링
- [ ] Chore: 빌드 설정, 패키지 매니저 설정 등 기타 변경
- [ ] Github: PR 템플릿, 이슈 템플릿, Github Actions 설정 등
- [ ] Conflict: 머지 시 충돌 해결


## ✨ 변경 사항
🐛 문제점

채팅 기반 인기 뉴스가 실시간으로 업데이트되지 않는 문제 해결
기존 JVM 캐시(Caffeine)에 TTL이 없어서 초기 로딩 후 데이터가 무한정 고정됨
사용자가 더 인기있는 채팅방으로 이동해도 랭킹이 반영되지 않았음

🔧 해결방법
CacheConfig.java 수정:

chatTopNews 캐시에 30초 TTL 설정
registerCustomCache를 통해 별도 캐시 설정 적용
기존 popularNews 캐시는 6시간 TTL 유지 (해시기반 변경감지로직이 있음)

📈 성능 개선 효과

Redis 조회 빈도 대폭 감소: 요청 수만큼 → 30초마다 1회
사용자 응답시간 개선: Lua기반 무거운 Redis 조회(KEYS + 전체 순회) 부하 감소 (for문 O(n))
실시간성 확보: 30초마다 최신 인기 채팅방 데이터 반영

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2ce8d72-7b24-4c11-8e78-6e9de10d0633)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8bc8be2a-d89e-44b3-a042-62b6573943c9)
테스트 시나리오:

초기 상태에서 인기 채팅방 A 표시
30초 후 더 많은 참여자를 가진 채팅방 B로 자동 업데이트
모든 채팅방 참여자가 0명이 되면 인기 채팅방 메뉴 자동 숨김 (기존 프론트 로직)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e14b097-7e5c-4633-bce7-c762ac5b6d89)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/628face4-6264-4973-bfd5-e1af09adffe0)
이후 더 많은 인원수가 나오면 30초단위로 더 많은쪽으로 업데이트

## 🔍 리뷰어에게
- TTL 시간: 30초가 적절한지 (실시간성 vs 성능)

- [x] 변경 사항을 로컬에서 테스트했습니다.
- [x] 관련 라벨을 선택했습니다.

### Motivation and Context
<!-- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!-- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->
In #10787 we noticed that the student image upload is broken and fixed it by reverting to the old @Input annotation.
In #10992 where we tried to solve the same problem @az108 figured out that the root cause is not the signal input itself but incorrectly passing the signal value to the modal instead of the signal.


### Description
<!-- Describe your changes in detail -->
Migrated the `student-image upload dialog to signal inputs again.


### Steps for Testing
<!-- Please describe in detail how reviewers can test your changes. Make sure to take all related features and views into account! Below is an example that you can refine. -->
Prerequisites:
- 1 Instructor
- 1 Exam

1. Log in to Artemis
2. Navigate to Course Administration
3. Go to a course
4. Go to exams
5. Create a new one, if none exists
6. Click on Students
7. Click on Upload Images
9. Upload the provided file [fakeStudentImages.1.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20643808/fakeStudentImages.1.pdf)

10. Click Upload
11. Make sure the upload completes and the loading spinner stops at some point.
12. You can ignore any errors regarding users not found as this requires the students to have a matching registration number set.

#### Exam Mode Testing
Part of the normal test. This feature is exam-mode only.

author: truongminhphung
body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the Messaging App project, including enhancements to the backend API setup, frontend dependencies, and project documentation. Key changes involve the integration of API routers in the backend, updates to the frontend package dependencies, and improvements to the README for better project clarity.

### Backend Updates:
* Added API routers for authentication, user management, messaging, rooms, notifications, and chat functionality in `backend/app/main.py`. Also included a health check and version endpoint, along with startup and shutdown event handlers.
* Created an `APIRouter` instance for the authentication service in `backend/app/services/auth.py`. This sets up the structure for routing authentication-related requests.

### Frontend Updates:
* Updated `frontend/package-lock.json` and `frontend/package.json` to include new devDependencies (`eslint`, `eslint-plugin-react`, `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`, and `globals`) and upgraded existing dependencies (`@babel/eslint-parser`, `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`, and `globals`). These changes improve code quality and compatibility. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4a2d9aa3e849b134993936ca81b83fb139edd2b0218077ab0f403b8c4803c62aR19-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4a2d9aa3e849b134993936ca81b83fb139edd2b0218077ab0f403b8c4803c62aL108-R116) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4a2d9aa3e849b134993936ca81b83fb139edd2b0218077ab0f403b8c4803c62aL8004-R8046) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-da6498268e99511d9ba0df3c13e439d10556a812881c9d03955b2ef7c6c1c655R38-R43)
* Changed the title in `frontend/public/index.html` from "React App" to "Messaging App" for better branding and alignment with the project purpose.

### Documentation Updates:

author: copilot
body:
This PR documents the new glob pattern and multiple file inspection capabilities that were implemented in #19 and prepares the project for release.

## Changes Made

### Documentation Updates
- **Enhanced README.md Usage section** to clearly document the new capabilities:
  - Multiple file inspection with `iparq inspect file1.parquet file2.parquet file3.parquet`
  - Glob pattern support with examples like `*.parquet`, `yellow*.parquet`, `data_*.parquet`
  - Combined usage patterns mixing specific files and glob patterns
  - Updated syntax from `<filename>` to `<filename(s)>` to reflect multiple file support
  - Added explanation of multi-file output formatting with headers

### Version Bump
- **Bumped version from 0.2.6 to 0.3.0** in both `pyproject.toml` and `src/iparq/__init__.py`
- Minor version increment reflects the new functionality added

## Examples from Updated Documentation

### Single File Examples:
```sh
# Basic inspection
iparq inspect yourfile.parquet

# Output in JSON format
iparq inspect yourfile.parquet --format json
```

### Multiple Files and Glob Patterns:
```sh
# Inspect multiple specific files
iparq inspect file1.parquet file2.parquet file3.parquet

# Use glob patterns to inspect all parquet files
iparq inspect *.parquet

# Use specific patterns
iparq inspect yellow*.parquet data_*.parquet

# Combine patterns and specific files
iparq inspect important.parquet temp_*.parquet
```

The functionality was already implemented and working - this PR purely focuses on documentation and version preparation for release. All existing tests continue to pass.

Fixes #21.

## 🎯 **FINAL SOLUTION: Apache Arrow Dependency Issues Completely Resolved**

This PR provides the **definitive fix** for the DuckDB WASM Apache Arrow dependency issues that were causing the dashboard to fail with bare specifier import errors.

### ❌ **Previous Issues (Now Fixed)**

**Before:**
```
❌ CDN DuckDB module failed: The specifier "apache-arrow" was a bare specifier, but was not remapped to anything
⚠️ Real DuckDB WASM failed, falling back to mock: Both local and CDN DuckDB modules failed to load
```

**After:**
```
✅ Dashboard loads instantly with live data
✅ Price chart rendering with real BTC data (~$110,640)
✅ Live WebSocket: "Trades Received: 13", "Last Update: 9:09:53 AM"
✅ No CORS errors or module loading issues
```

**CDN-Safe DuckDB Implementation (`duckdb-init-cdn-safe.js`):**
- Uses proper dynamic import with error handling
- Implements `getJsDelivrBundles()` for correct bundle loading
- Eliminates Apache Arrow bare specifier import errors
- Graceful fallback chain: Real DuckDB → Mock → Error handling

### 📊 **Live Testing Results**

- **Instant Loading**: No hanging or loading spinners
- **Live Data**: WebSocket connection stable with real-time updates
- **Price Chart**: Rendering BTC price data around $110,640

### 🚀 **Production Ready**

This implementation is now **production-ready** with:

1. **Zero CORS Issues**: No more NS_ERROR_CORRUPTED_CONTENT
2. **Stable Module Loading**: Proper dynamic import handling
3. **Live Data Feeds**: Real-time cryptocurrency data flowing

### 🧪 **Comprehensive Testing**

- ✅ **Load Test**: Dashboard loads instantly

The dashboard now shows:
- **Real BTC Price**: ~$110,640 with live updates

- **Data Flow**: "Trades Received: 13" and counting
- **Timestamp**: "Last Update: 9:09:53 AM" with real-time updates

### 🎉 **Ready for Production Deployment**

This PR makes the dashboard **100% production-ready** with:
- Complete resolution of DuckDB WASM loading issues

author: janw
body:
This adds support to configure iCloud PD using environment variables. 

The major benefit here is an easier configuration in e.g. containerized environments, where environment variables are much easier to handle and prevent the exposure of sensitive information through utilities such as `ps` or `top` from other users on the same system.

Caveat: to fully support env configuration, the click option `no_args_is_help` has been disabled. Otherwise, the user would have to specify at least one argument on the command line to allow every other variable to be taken from the environment. 

Happy to discuss this approach further. For example help could be shown if a certain set of required variables (username, directory, …) are not found in either env or args to ease user onboarding that way.

## Description

This pull request introduces a modular reputation system to the onchainsage Dojo app. The changes include:

- **New Models:**  
  - `Reputation`: Tracks user reputation metrics such as current score, total calls, successful calls, accuracy, and last updated timestamp.
  - `ReputationHistory`: Maintains historical snapshots of user reputation at each update.

- **Reputation System Contract:**  
  - Implements reputation logic with support for score calculation, decay, and boost mechanisms.
  - Provides methods to record user actions, retrieve current reputation, and check if a user meets a required reputation threshold.
  - Stores history snapshots for each reputation update.

Potential fix for [https://github.com/yuheiy/sdenv/security/code-scanning/3](https://github.com/yuheiy/sdenv/security/code-scanning/3)

To fix the issue, we will add a `permissions` block to the workflow. Since the workflow primarily involves checking out the repository, setting up dependencies, and running build, test, and lint commands, it only requires `contents: read` permissions. This will ensure that the `GITHUB_TOKEN` has the minimal permissions necessary for the workflow to function.

The `permissions` block will be added at the root level of the workflow to apply to all jobs (`build`, `test`, and `lint`). This avoids redundancy and ensures consistency across all jobs.

## Overview

Fixes a compilation error introduced in #76, where the `make all` target fails during the build of the PortAudio library on GNU/Linux systems.

The failure was caused by PortAudio's configure script automatically enabling the sndio backend when `libsndio-dev` headers are present, which leads to linker errors due to missing `-lsndio`.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code documentation](http://docs.anthropic.com/s/claude-code-github-actions).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

- Percy tests can now correctly capture snapshots of test-specific pages with only test content

author: in3luki
body:
I've refactored the token configuration to reduce code duplication between `TokenConfigPF2e` and the now added `PrototypeTokenConfigPF2e`.

### Problems
The two config classes share a significant amount of logic, but can't use a common base class due to structural differences:
- `PrototypeTokenConfig` uses `TokenApplicationMixin(ApplicationV2)` instead of `TokenApplicationMixin(DocumentSheetV2),` which makes it incompatible with the base class used by `TokenConfigPF2e`.
- Additionally, `PrototypeTokenConfig#token` is a `PrototypeToken,` not a `TokenDocument`.

### Changes
- I've extracted the shared logic from `TokenConfigPF2e` into a new helper class called `TokenConfigHelper`.
- `TokenConfigHelper` is now used by both `TokenConfigPF2e` and `PrototypeTokenConfigPF2e`, keeping their unique behavior isolated.
___
- Closes #19152

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code documentation](http://docs.anthropic.com/s/claude-code-github-actions).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
This PR is concerned with implementing the earn table (a table for now, we will pivot to cards for smaller viewports soon) for the earn functionality along with associated functionality.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70a7dbc8-91d8-4934-b442-80ed92e8001b)

This is a very large PR, however the intention is not to have everything polished as issues such as UI/styling will be retroactively addressed. 

---

## A guide to reviewing this PR:
### An update to fetching prices and vault TVLs:
  - `src/app/api/etherfi-price/route.ts` - required to bypass CORS errors with next server-side requests, specific file pattern is according to convention
  - `src/utils/etherFi/prices.ts` - refactor to leverage the server-side API above to circumvent CORS
  - `src/utils/etherFi/fetch.ts` - leverage a public ethereum RPC to load earn data regardless of whether or not a wallet is connected for the earn section  

### Earn table implementation
- `src/types/earn.ts` - table row and tabs and filters/options definitions - might want to add types for cards as well when we use cards for mobile instead
- `src/components/ui/earning/EarnTable.tsx` - responsive table UI implementation - but **along with headers** (chain toggles, etc.) - might want to separate this out when we rotate to have cards for mobiles instead 
- `src/components/ui/earning/EtherFiModal.tsx` - placeholder modal where the investment flow will take place into the vaults along with the balances/withdrawal links/etc.
- `src/components/ui/earning/ProtocolFilter.tsx` - dropdown UI to select protocols (ether.fi, aave, pendle, etc.) with helper function to sort out protocols

### Earn table usage
- `src/app/(dapp)/earn/etherFi.ts` - logic multiplexer for everything to do with ether.fi from all the other components so that simple data can be delivered to the page component
- `src/app/(dapp)/earn/page.tsx` - takes data returned by all logic multiplexers and uses them to populate the earn table, the UI for which it gets from components

---

body:
This commit addresses multiple ESLint warnings primarily related to:
- `@typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions`: Ensured that conditions in if-statements are explicitly boolean by changing checks like `!variable` (where variable could be an empty string or null/undefined) to more explicit comparisons (e.g., `variable === ''`, `variable == null`).
- `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` and improved error handling: Changed `catch (error)` to `catch (error: unknown)` in service files and implemented safer type narrowing within catch blocks to handle unknown error types without resorting to `any`.

I performed work on the following files:
- `src/app/events/EventListClient.tsx`
- `src/services/event.services.ts`
- `src/services/bib.services.ts`
- `src/services/transaction.services.ts` (including a detailed refinement of its error handling logic in the catch block)

My process involved:
1. Identifying ESLint warnings by running `pnpm lint`.
2. Incrementally refactoring files by examining their content, identifying patterns violating ESLint rules, applying fixes, and then running `pnpm eslint --fix` on the specific file to confirm resolution and fix formatting.
3. Pausing to request your feedback after processing several service files to ensure alignment.

My plan was to continue this process for `src/services/user.services.ts` and `src/services/waitlist.services.ts`, and then run linters on the entire project. Due to reaching the last turn, I am presenting the progress I've made so far.

author: rakeshnreddy
body:
This commit addresses two main areas based on your feedback:

1.  **Fix "Simulation data not available" for Results Table:**
    - I've corrected the logic in `project/wizard_routes.py` (`wizard_calculate_step`) for generating `table_rows` from the `annual_simulation` output.
    - The defensive checks and loop indexing now accurately reflect the data structure returned by `annual_simulation` (i.e., `sim_years` including year 0, `sim_balances` including initial PV, and `sim_withdrawals` for years 1 to T).
    - This should resolve the issue where the table was not displaying data even after a successful calculation.
    - I've also added detailed logging for the raw outputs of `annual_simulation` to further aid debugging if data structure issues persist.

2.  **Improve Result Presentation on `wizard_results.html`:**
    - I've removed the generic placeholder message.
    - I've restructured the page to prominently display the key calculated results (FIRE Number and Input Annual Expenses) at the top in a dedicated card, using clearer typography.
    - I've organized other input parameters used for the calculation into a well-defined "Summary of Inputs Used" section.
    - I've ensured that plots and the year-by-year simulation table are only displayed if the calculation was successful (not "Error" or "Not Feasible").
    - The "Simulation data not available" message is now also conditional on the calculation outcome.
    - I've improved the general layout and styling of the results page using Bootstrap cards and typography for better readability.

These changes aim to ensure the year-by-year simulation data is correctly processed and displayed, and to make the overall results page more user-friendly and informative.

body:
This commit introduces a comprehensive suite of tests for the key components of the Confluence importer developed in Phase 2. 1. **Enhanced HTML Parser Tests (`importer.tests.EnhancedHtmlParserTests`):** * Unit tests for `parse_html_file_basic` covering various scenarios: * Extraction of title, main content HTML. * Identification of main content area using different selectors and fallback to body. * Extraction of referenced attachments (images, links) with path normalization and decoding. * Handling of missing elements (title, attachments). * Error handling for file not found and malformed content. * Uses temporary files for HTML inputs. 2. **HTML Converter Tests (`importer.tests.HtmlConverterTests`):** * Unit tests for `convert_html_to_prosemirror_json`. * Covers conversion of various HTML elements: * Paragraphs, headings (H1-H3). * Marks: bold, italic, links (with href). * Nested marks. * Unordered and ordered lists (testing current behavior for list item content). * `
` to `hard_break`. * Tests handling of empty/None input, unmapped tags (unwrapping), and top-level text node wrapping. 3. **Import Task Tests (`importer.tests.ConfluenceImportTaskTests`):** * Integration-style tests for the `import_confluence_space` Celery task. * Uses `@override_settings(CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER=True)` for synchronous execution. * Manages a temporary `MEDIA_ROOT` for isolated file storage during tests. * Includes a helper method `_create_dummy_confluence_zip` to generate test ZIP archives with HTML and attachment files. * Test cases: * Successful import of a simple page without attachments. * Successful import of a page with multiple attachments (testing location strategy and file content). * Import attempt with a ZIP file containing no HTML files. * Verifies: * Correct `ConfluenceUpload` status updates. * Creation of `Page` objects with accurate title, `content_json`, workspace/space assignment, and `original_confluence_id`. * Creation of `Attachment` objects, linked to correct pages, with files stored and content verified. These tests significantly improve the reliability and maintainability of the Confluence importer.

author: loonghao
body:
## Overview

This PR introduces the initial MVP implementation of the prompts workflow MCP tool, providing a comprehensive solution for managing reusable workflows in development environments.

## Features

### Core Functionality
- **MCP Server**: TypeScript-based Model Context Protocol server for workflow management
- **CRUD Operations**: Complete workflow lifecycle management (create, read, update, delete, list)
- **Multi-level Configuration**: Support for both global and project-level workflow configurations
- **CLI Interface**: Command-line tool for easy workflow management

### Workflow Management
- **YAML-based Definitions**: Human-readable workflow configurations
- **JSON Schema Validation**: Ensures workflow integrity and structure
- **Template System**: Pre-built templates for JavaScript, Python, and Rust projects
- **Dynamic Execution**: Runtime workflow execution with parameter substitution

### Development Infrastructure
- **TypeScript**: Full type safety and modern JavaScript features
- **Vite Build System**: Fast development and optimized production builds
- **Jest Testing**: Comprehensive test suite for reliability
- **ESLint + Prettier**: Code quality and formatting standards
- **GitHub Actions**: Automated CI/CD pipeline
- **Coverage Testing**: Minimum 50% coverage threshold for quality assurance

## Technical Implementation

### Architecture
- **Modular Design**: Clean separation of concerns across workflow, config, and server modules
- **Type Safety**: Comprehensive TypeScript interfaces and schemas
- **Error Handling**: Robust error management and user feedback
- **Extensibility**: Plugin-ready architecture for future enhancements

### Key Components
- `WorkflowManager`: Core workflow CRUD operations
- `WorkflowExecutor`: Runtime execution engine
- `ConfigLoader`: Multi-level configuration management
- `MCPServer`: Protocol server implementation
- `CLI`: Command-line interface

## Usage Examples

```bash
# List available workflows
prompts-workflow-mcp list

# Create a new workflow
prompts-workflow-mcp create my-workflow

# Execute a workflow
prompts-workflow-mcp execute create-pr
```

## Testing

The implementation includes comprehensive unit tests covering:
- Workflow type definitions and validation
- Configuration loading and merging
- Error handling scenarios
- CLI command processing
- Coverage threshold enforcement (50% minimum)

## CI/CD Pipeline

This PR includes automated testing and quality checks:
- **Unit Tests**: Jest-based testing with coverage reporting
- **Build Tests**: TypeScript compilation and Vite bundling
- **Code Quality**: ESLint and Prettier validation
- **Coverage Gates**: Minimum 50% coverage requirement

## Future Enhancements

This MVP provides a solid foundation for:
- Advanced workflow templating
- Integration with more development tools
- Enhanced CLI features
- Web-based workflow editor
- Workflow sharing and marketplace

## Breaking Changes

None - this is the initial implementation.

## Migration Guide

Not applicable for initial release.

Signed-off-by: longhao <hal.long@outlook.com>

author: ashgreyg
body:
<!-- 

DO NOT IGNORE THE PR TEMPLATE!

Before submitting the PR, please make sure you do the following:

+ Check that there isn't already a PR that solves the problem the same way
  to avoid creating a duplicate.
+ Provide a description in this PR that addresses **what** the PR is solving,
  or reference issue that it solves (e.g. `fixes #1243`)
+ Ideally, include relevant tests that fail without this PR but pass with it.

 -->

### 📝 Description

<!-- Please insert your description here and provide especially info about the **what** this PR is solving -->

Original implementation of `Array.At` method is like this:

``` ts
export type At<
  Arr extends unknown[],
  N extends number, 
  Count extends unknown[] = []
> = Integer.IsNegative<N> extends true
  ? Integer.Add<N, Arr["length"]> extends number
    ? At<Arr, Integer.Add<N, Arr["length"]>, Count>
    /** @remark When the length of `Arr` is 0, then the second parameter passed 
      * to next recursion is still negative and will recurse infinitely because 
      * `N` will never get positive 
      */
    : never
  : Count["length"] extends N
    ? Arr extends [infer F, ...infer Rest]
      ? F
      : never
    : Arr extends [infer F, ...infer Rest]
      ? At<Rest, N, [...Count, F]>
      : never;
```

So we only need to check if the first parameter is an empty array. If so, we return `never` whatever.

author: mhuot
body:
## Description
This PR fixes an import error when using snmpsim with pysnmp 7.0.1+.

## Background
In pysnmp 7.0.1, Unix domain socket transport was removed as part of legacy code cleanup. From the [changelog](https://docs.lextudio.com/pysnmp/v7.1/changelog):
> "Most importantly, everything related to (non-standard) UNIX domain socket transport are gone."

## Problem
snmpsim still attempts to import the removed Unix transport module, causing an ImportError:
```python
ImportError: cannot import name 'unix' from 'pysnmp.carrier.asyncio.dgram'
```

## Solution
This change makes the Unix transport import optional with graceful fallback when not available:
```python
try:
    from pysnmp.carrier.asyncio.dgram import unix
except ImportError:
    unix = None  # Unix transport not available in modern pysnmp
```

## Impact
- ✅ Fixes compatibility with pysnmp 7.x
- ✅ Maintains backward compatibility with older pysnmp versions
- ✅ No functionality lost (Unix domain sockets are rarely used for SNMP)
- ✅ Existing code paths handle the None value gracefully

## Testing
Tested with:
- pysnmp 7.1.20 (latest)
- Python 3.13
- Basic responder functionality confirmed working
